outcomes: Initiated in 2009 as a community-driven collaboration between the Powel family, Bainbridge Island Land Trust, and state and federal salmon recovery funders, the project removed approximately one-third of a mile of aging bulkheads and over 1,340 tons of riprap, concrete, and creosote timber. Over 2,500 native plants were installed, invasive species cleared, and intertidal habitat expanded by roughly 163%. A diverse stakeholder group—ranging from tribal representatives to city, engineering, and ecological experts guided the design process, supported by 1,200+ volunteer hours. The project also restored intertidal and salt marsh habitat, benefiting salmon and other wildlife.
